instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest, palms facing forward.
2. Flare your elbows out and lower the dumbbells in an arc toward your chest.
3. Bring the dumbbells together just above your chest, elbows pointing out.
4. Press the dumbbells back up by extending your elbows to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
2. Move slowly and under control, no momentum.
3. Keep the dumbbells facing forward through the full range.
4. Use a moderate weight so the elbows stay stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, supporting your left hand on your left knee.
3. Raise your right elbow until the upper arm is parallel to the floor, forearm hanging down.
4. Extend your elbow to straighten the arm behind you, keeping the upper arm still.
5. Lower the dumbbell back under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm pinned and motionless throughout.
2. Move slowly and squeeze the triceps at full extension.
3. Do not swing the weight; drive only with the triceps.
4. Keep your back flat and core braced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Raise the upper arm until the elbow is level with the shoulder, bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing down.
3. Keep the elbow fixed and rotate the forearm upward until it points up.
4. Rotate the forearm slowly back down to the start, then switch arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light dumbbell to keep form clean.
2. Move slowly and control the rotation.
3. Keep the elbow fixed at shoulder height.
4. Drive the movement from the shoulder, not momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back, legs straight, holding a dumbbell with both hands and arms extended overhead on the floor.
2. Lift your legs, upper body, and the dumbbell at the same time into a V shape.
3. Reach the dumbbell toward your feet, keeping arms and legs straight.
4. Lower your legs, torso, and dumbbell back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms and legs straight to maximize the contraction.
2. Exhale as you fold up, inhale as you lower.
3. Move under control, no jerking or momentum.
4. Keep your lower back from arching off the floor.
